newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slip on fuel price hike speculation.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slip on fuel price hike speculation.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange tumbled on late selling by speculators on Tuesday amid expectations the government may raise the prices of petroleum products ahead of the budget next week, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 8.41 points lower at 747.62.
"The mounting deficit in the country's oil pool account, which may force the government to announce a hike in petroleum product prices, fuelled the selling," said one broker.
India's oil pool deficit, representing what the government owes oil companies from its price subsidy programme, stands at an estimated 155 billion rupees.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front government has been considering a fuel price increase for the past few months but its coalition partners have resisted the move.
The government raised fuel product prices by an average 15 percent last July after just a month in office, prompting protests from the opposition and left-wing coalition parties.
Another broker said the drop in share prices was expected by the market after the rise of last few sessions.
"The fall in share prices was a technical correction as some stocks were in overbought position," said Ajit Sial of brokers Sial and Company.
Reliance Industries closed 5.00 rupees lower at 272.25 on selling by speculators, brokers said.
ACC quoted 26.90 rupees lower at 1,419 on profit-taking by speculators.
Larsen and Toubro shed 2.55 rupees to 245.95.
ITC slipped 9.50 rupees to 417.25 on foreign selling.
